explanation: An array stores a fixed number of elements of one type. Indices start at zero. If the array has N elements, N itself is outside the valid range.
exampleExplanation: The last valid index is 2, so last is initialized to 6.
misconceptions: C does not automatically stop an out-of-bounds access.
An array expression often converts to a pointer to its first element. A pointer parameter does not carry the array length.

reference.title: Local C reference on elements and bounds
reference.text: Index expressions must refer to an element within the array when dereferenced. Pass the length separately when a function receives a pointer to the first element. Check the length before using indices derived from external input.
